clauses.reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 10878 in the number column of the table (the text layer separates the number column from the subject column for this part of the table, so its subject text is not quoted). This order (25 FR 4575, Federal Register of May 25, 1960, signed May 23, 1960) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Chicago, Rock Island and Pacific Railroad Company and other carriers represented by the Western Carriers' Conference Committee (listed in attached List A) and certain of their employees represented by the Switchmen's Union of North America, AFL-CIO; barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by June 22, 1960); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by those carriers or by their employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. A held lead copy of the report of Emergency Board No. 131 (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated July 8, 1960; the report states that the parties stipulated to request an extension of time to July 15, 1960. Thirty days after July 8, 1960 is August 7, 1960. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on July 8, 1960, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on August 7, 1960.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (25 FR 4575, the issue of May 25, 1960) is the order itself: it is headed Executive Order 10878, and it creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for the dispute described in the clause, and is dated May 23, 1960. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C): a report deadline and a spent standstill are not ends. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit naming this order. The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553.

savings.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The commands of this order were one-time commands tied to one labor dispute, and no held claim-grade source shows any of them continuing when it was revoked. The statute the order applied, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160), is a separate source of law and does not depend on this order.
